decisions.reason: Conferencing is a commoditised add-on now facing hyperscaler collaboration tools after the pandemic, and with no observed traction since 2018 its value looks less likely to materialise, though it is still cheap enough to keep for now.
Early adoption by data centres and financial hubs, plus a close fit with the owned metro fibre and data centre strategy, justifies continued commitment.
Optical spectrum runs on owned fibre, fits the high-bandwidth direction and serves growing hyperscaler demand, so the option keeps rising in value at low holding cost.
A self-service number ordering portal supports real-time provisioning of the voice business at low marginal cost, though it may be absorbed into a broader platform.
Carrier pre-selection is a legacy service in a shrinking market with the move to all-IP, so uncertainty has resolved against it and the freed resources are better used in software-defined services.
Direct voice network connection is core to enterprise voice on the owned network and is cheap to maintain, so there is no reason to abandon it.
